subject.title: fix(browser): prove post-action target continuity before adopting a tab

question: Should OpenClaw make stale target IDs plus explicit re-selection the public recovery contract whenever browser backends cannot prove post-action continuity, rather than preserving inferred continuation behavior?
rationale: This is a deliberate compatibility and workflow tradeoff: the safer failure mode prevents wrong-tab mutation, while some existing callers may lose transparent continuation after replacement or detach/reattach.

options.title: Accept fail-safe recovery
options.body: Adopt backend-owned identity when available and otherwise return the acted-on stale target so callers must obtain a fresh explicit selection.

options.title: Require stable relay continuity first
options.body: Pause this route-contract change until the relay exposes a stable operation-owned handle that preserves continuation across supported detach/reattach cases.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-safe recovery
recommendation.body: Adopt backend-owned identity when available and otherwise return the acted-on stale target so callers must obtain a fresh explicit selection.

likelyOwner.reason: The canonical report and PR discussion both identify this as a browser continuity-contract decision requiring their direction.
